newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon economic growth slows in Feb - Bank.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon economic growth slows in Feb - Bank.

text.p: The growth of economic activity in Lebanon dipped in February to its lowest level in 10 months, the Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin on Tuesday.
The central bank said its coincident indicator of economic activity stood at 161.4 against 166.0 in January, and above its 150.2 level in February 1996.
It was the indicator's lowest level since dipping to 150.1 in April 1996 when Israel carried out a 17-day blitz on the country, killing about 200 people and causing widespread damage.
"The Banque Du Liban coincident indicator stood at 161.4 in February against 166.0 in January suggesting a slowdown in economic activity, in part due to seasonal factors," the bank said.

The coincident indicator combines 12 economic series including imports, exports, electricity output and airport and port activity but the bank has not revealed the weighting of the different series and some economists question its value.
The bank created the indicator in 1993 because of a lack of reliable data in Lebanon which prevents precise calculation of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and economic growth.
